title: CloudBQ - HubSpot new-deals pipeline on Cloud Run and BigQuery
one_liner: Weekly HubSpot new-deals report: a Cloud Run function lands raw deals in BigQuery and CALLs one stored procedure that scores, de-duplicates and MERGEs them; three orchestrator lanes compared.
purpose: Stage/probability reports cannot see a deal for weeks after it is created, so this layer reports every HubSpot deal created since the last successful run, per entity (SEALSQ, ICALPS), with a day-1 hot score and a cross-pipeline duplicate flag, into hubspot.new_deals plus a weekly XLSX/e-mail. Three candidate orchestrators are scaffolded side by side so the choice is made on evidence: A a Cloud Run function driven by Cloud Scheduler, B n8n on Cloud Run (kept only as the delivery tail B1), C a hybrid of BigQuery scheduled queries over a synced copy of HubSpot plus a Node 22 Cloud Run job that writes the score back. Since pass 3 every lane lands its inputs in a run_ts-keyed raw root (deals_raw / labels_raw) and CALLs the same procedure new_deals_batch, so any past run can be recomputed from BigQuery. Pass 2 adds L2 likelihood tiers per deal and a company rollup. The repo also carries four reusable documentation/scaffolding skills. Nothing has run against Google Cloud yet: every step is rehearsed offline.
domain: CRM analytics pipeline (HubSpot to BigQuery on GCP)
stack: BigQuery standard SQL (procedure, table function, UDF, JSON)
BigQuery Data Transfer Service (scheduled queries, HubSpot connector)
n8n 2.41.7 on Cloud Run + Cloud SQL Postgres 17
aliases: the Cloud Run to BigQuery thing

architecture.component: Lane A - Cloud Run function new_deals_report
architecture.responsibility: Extract and land only: reads the watermark, takes a lease, searches HubSpot for deals created in the window, lands them in deals_raw/labels_raw, CALLs new_deals_batch, reads the result back, advances the watermark, POSTs the payload to the delivery webhook.
The single execution surface of lane A: create-or-update steps for APIs, IAM, tables, routines, secret, deploy, Scheduler jobs (created paused), plus the dry gate, run, replay, probe, status, logs.

DDL for report_state (watermark + lock_until lease), new_deals (sink, MERGE key deal_id), new_deals_runs (one row per run, data_gaps), new_deals_history (per-run slice), deals_raw / labels_raw (the raw root) and the view new_deals_last_7d.
View deals_landed_v1 types the landed JSON once with SAFE_CAST and computes name_key; table function new_deals_batch_rows returns the shaped, scored, de-duplicated batch of one run, read-only.

architecture.component: The one write path: procedure new_deals_batch
architecture.responsibility: Stored procedure every lane CALLs after landing: TEMP batch, then one transaction of MERGE new_deals, history slice, runs row and (if asked) report_state; dry mode writes only one runs row; any error rolls back, writes a FAILED row and re-raises.

BigQuery UDF returning STRUCT<score, hot, raw>: a logistic score over eight features, hot when >= 45, NULL for pipelines without a conversion rate. Constants live once in scoring/hot_score_v1.constants.json; Python hot_score() is only the test oracle.

architecture.component: Lane C - scheduled compute over the sync
architecture.responsibility: BigQuery scheduled script per entity: 36 h freshness guard on the synced deals, lands the 90-day set from the sync table (land_raw.sql), then CALLs new_deals_batch with advance_state = TRUE on its own state row NEW_DEALS_<entity>_C.

architecture.component: Lane C - sync adapters and ranking views
architecture.responsibility: Adapter views over the HubSpot to BigQuery transfer (deals_synced_v1, owners_synced_v1, pipeline label views); sql/hot_deals_v1.sql ranks open deals per region and exposes hot_deals_v1_writeback, the delta the write-back must PATCH.

Reads hot_deals_v1_writeback, PATCHes hot_score_v1 / hot_flag_v1 onto HubSpot deals in batches of 100 with 429/5xx backoff, logs one row per deal to writeback_log; dry unless WRITEBACK_APPROVE=1; never sends a NULL score.

Generates NEW_DEALS_DELIVERY (webhook with Header Auth, rows to XLSX to e-mail, text-only e-mail on a zero-row week) and NEW_DEALS_ERRORS; deploy/n8n/ holds the Cloud Run service manifest, Cloud SQL, secrets and import scripts.

Classifies every deal by certainty with RANGE_BUCKET on edges 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.9 into Tier4..Tier1 or Closed_won / Closed_lost; deal_tiers_apply.sql is the scheduled MERGE into the gold table deal_tiers with history and retirement.

One CTE chain resolving each deal to a company through five resolvers in precedence, spliced into the views of company_tiers_v1.sql and into the notebook dry run; company_tiers_apply.sql refreshes the snapshot in one transaction.

cloudbq_deploy_and_witness.ipynb runs the deploy.sh sequence cell by cell and witnesses the SQL from Python; l2_deal_tiers.ipynb is the tier lab (numpy.digitize vs RANGE_BUCKET); company_tiers.ipynb is the dry-run, ship, gate probe of pass 2b.

The lane matrix source: layers L0-L17 across lanes A/B/C/R with a parity word, remediation rows and equality checks; built into docs/EXECUTION_SURFACES.xlsx; docs/EXECUTION_SURFACES.md is the append-only timeline.

Four project-agnostic skills under .claude/skills/: aider-scaffold (recipes + diff ledger), tree-f-visualizer (architecture tree), pass-sequence (sequence page, record, workbook), regen-workflow (generator-then-commit GitHub Actions); plus discovery and implementation agent definitions.

On push and PR: pytest, bash -n on every script, node --check, build_workflow --check, workbook --verify, tree --check, ledger --check, README index --check and a DRYRUN=1 rehearsal of deploy.sh all and dry.

data_flow: 1. Cloud Scheduler (Mon 07:00 SEALSQ, 07:20 ICALPS, Europe/Zurich) sends GET <url>?entity=E with an OIDC token of the function's service account to the private Cloud Run service.
2. new_deals_report truncates now to the second as run_ts, loads pipeline/stage/owner labels from HubSpot, and reads the watermark from report_state (first run: now minus FIRST_RUN_DAYS = 7).
3. A live window run takes the lease with one atomic UPDATE of report_state.lock_until; if another run holds it the function answers 409 and writes nothing. Dry runs take no lease.
4. HubSpot search: deals with createdate in [watermark - OVERLAP_MINUTES (5), run_ts), all pipelines; the entity's pipelines are in scope, the rest are kept as duplicate candidates.

5. Landing (the raw root): land_raw load-jobs the whole search result into deals_raw with properties as JSON and in_scope per deal, land_labels does the same for labels_raw; each loads first, then deletes older rows of the same (run_ts, entity, orchestrator) key. A landing failure fails the run (raw_landing_failed).

6. call_batch submits ONE statement, CALL new_deals_batch(run_ts, entity, orchestrator, mode, FALSE, NULL, watermark_in, query_start, query_end, started_ms, gaps), and waits up to CALL_TIMEOUT_S (240 s), cancelling the job on timeout.

7. Inside BigQuery the procedure builds a TEMP batch from new_deals_batch_rows (typed view, labels, hot_score_v1, duplicates over a 90-day horizon), then in one transaction MERGEs new_deals on deal_id (four frozen columns untouched), replaces the history slice and writes the runs row.

8. read_batch reads the run's rows back from new_deals_history (dry: from the table function) plus rows_written and data_gaps from the runs row; only then write_watermark sets watermark = run_ts and clears the lease in one statement.

9. The payload (report_id, window, row_count, rows_written, duplicate_suspects, day1_hot, data_gaps, rows) is returned and, on live runs, POSTed to DELIVERY_WEBHOOK_URL with three tries; a failed delivery amends the runs row to OK_DELIVERY_FAILED.
10. n8n NEW_DEALS_DELIVERY (lane B1) receives the payload behind Header Auth, builds the XLSX and sends the e-mail, or a text-only e-mail when row_count is 0.

11. Lane C in parallel or as fallback: DTS sync daily 02:00 UTC, scheduled queries Mon 03:53 / 04:23 UTC land the 90-day set and CALL the same procedure with advance_state = TRUE, then the write-back job (Mon 05:30 Zurich) PATCHes hot_score_v1 / hot_flag_v1 onto deals.
12. On any exception the function marks the procedure's row FAILED (or writes its own FAILED row if none exists), releases the lease and re-raises, so the window stays replayable.

key_functions.name: new_deals_report
key_functions.does: HTTP entry point of lane A. Orchestrates lease, HubSpot search, landing, the CALL, read-back, watermark and delivery; decides the mode (window, event or dry) and returns (payload, 200). It is a synchronous request handler: there is no async def anywhere in the Python.
key_functions.expected_output: 200 with a payload where dry_run is true and rows_written is 0 (the assertion of deploy.sh dry); an unknown entity returns ({'error': 'unknown entity X'}, 400); an overlapping live run returns 409.

key_functions.name: call_batch
key_functions.signature: def call_batch(client, entity, run_ts, mode, window, started, gaps)
key_functions.does: The asynchronous hand-off to BigQuery: client.query() submits the CALL new_deals_batch as a BigQuery job, job.result(timeout=CALL_TIMEOUT_S) blocks on it, and on timeout the job is cancelled so a late procedure cannot land a surprise OK row. Passes advance_state = FALSE and literal NULLs for a missing window.
key_functions.expected_output: the CALL text ends with 'FALSE, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, @started_ms, @gaps)' and the gaps parameter is ['event_no_window'] (tests/test_main_offline.py:253)

key_functions.name: land_raw
key_functions.signature: def land_raw(client, found, in_scope_ids, entity, run_ts, mode, source="hubspot_api")
key_functions.does: Writes the raw root slice: a load job (load_table_from_json, WRITE_APPEND) of the whole search result into deals_raw, then a DELETE of older rows of the same key, both time-boxed by LAND_TIMEOUT_S. Returns (rows landed, whether an older slice was replaced).
key_functions.expected_output: For a search returning deals 1, 2, 3 where 1 and 3 belong to the entity: 3 rows landed, in_scope True for 1 and 3 and False for 2, source 'hubspot_api', properties a dict (tests/test_main_offline.py:306-314)

key_functions.name: acquire_lease
key_functions.does: One run per entity at a time: creates the report_state row on first run, then sets lock_until = run_ts + LEASE_MINUTES (12) with an UPDATE guarded by 'lock_until IS NULL OR lock_until < @ts'; returns True only when exactly one row was affected.
key_functions.expected_output: False when another run holds a live lease; the caller then answers 409 and no load and no CALL happen (tests/test_main_offline.py:238-240)

key_functions.name: write_watermark
key_functions.does: Advances report_state.watermark to run_ts and sets lock_until = NULL in one UPDATE. Called only for live window runs, after the CALL and the read-back succeeded, so a failed run leaves no gap.

key_functions.name: read_batch
key_functions.signature: def read_batch(client, entity, run_ts, mode, query_start=None, deal_ids=None)
key_functions.does: Renders the payload rows from the tables the run wrote: live runs read the history slice plus rows_written and data_gaps from the runs row; dry runs read the table function new_deals_batch_rows. Ordered by amount_kusd DESC, deal_id.
key_functions.expected_output: dry: (rows, 0, []); live: (rows, rows_written from the runs row, the procedure's data_gaps)

key_functions.name: hot_score
key_functions.does: Python test oracle of the day-1 hot score (not in the request path since pass 3): logistic of eight weighted features plus bias, 0-100, hot when >= 45. Only pipelines [id] and [id] are scored.
key_functions.input_example: vector hw_qualified_big_arr_2027: pipeline [id], stage probability 0.2, closedate 2027-03-31, ARR 16002, 3 contacted notes, revenue_state Pipeline, now 2026-10-05T07:00Z
key_functions.expected_output: (90.3, True); vector hw_identified_no_data gives (2.8, False); a non-scored pipeline gives (None, None) (tests/hot_score_vectors.json)

key_functions.name: name_key
key_functions.does: Duplicate key of a deal: final_customer if present, else the part of dealname before the first '-', '/', '|' or '(' ; lower-cased, non-alphanumerics removed, cut to 40 chars. The SQL twin lives in deals_landed_v1.

key_functions.name: new_deals_batch (procedure)
key_functions.signature: PROCEDURE new_deals_batch(p_run_ts TIMESTAMP, p_entity STRING, p_orchestrator STRING, p_mode STRING, p_advance_state BOOL, p_state_report_id STRING, p_watermark_in TIMESTAMP, p_query_start TIMESTAMP, p_query_end TIMESTAMP, p_started_ms INT64, p_gaps ARRAY<STRING>)
key_functions.does: The one write path. Validates mode, checks lane A's lease when advancing state, adds labels_missing / dedup_horizon_partial to the gaps, then MERGE + history + runs row (+ state with GREATEST) in one transaction; dry writes one runs row only.
key_functions.expected_output: exactly one new_deals_runs row with dry_run = TRUE and rows_written = 0; no MERGE, no history, no state

key_functions.name: new_deals_batch_rows (table function)
key_functions.signature: TABLE FUNCTION new_deals_batch_rows(p_run_ts TIMESTAMP, p_entity STRING, p_orchestrator STRING, p_window_start TIMESTAMP)
key_functions.does: The pure, read-only batch: in-scope deals of the slice (one row per deal, latest fetched_at), labels joined, hot_score_v1 applied with run_ts as now, duplicates from every deal the root knows within 90 days. Column order equals new_deals. Use it to debug a past run without writing.

key_functions.name: hot_score_v1 (UDF)
key_functions.signature: FUNCTION hot_score_v1(pipeline STRING, hs_deal_stage_probability FLOAT64, closedate TIMESTAMP, calculation___pipeline_2026__k__ FLOAT64, services_value_2026 FLOAT64, asp_in_usd_q2_2022_calculation FLOAT64, tpm__k_y FLOAT64, product_hierarchy STRING, num_contacted_notes FLOAT64, notes_last_updated TIMESTAMP, revenue_state STRING, run_ts TIMESTAMP) RETURNS STRUCT<score, hot, raw>
key_functions.does: THE implementation of the score since pass 3 (12 positional arguments, pinned by tests/test_pass3_sql.py). Returns NULL when the pipeline has no conversion rate.
key_functions.expected_output: Every row of tests/hot_score_vectors.sql shows ok = TRUE (15 vectors); offline DuckDB parity on 15 vectors + 4,000 random deals

key_functions.name: deploy (deploy.sh)
key_functions.signature: deploy()  # gcloud run deploy $FN --source . --function new_deals_report --base-image python312 --no-allow-unauthenticated --timeout 540 --memory 512Mi --max-instances 1 --concurrency 1
key_functions.does: Canonical Cloud Run function deploy from source: private service, one instance, one request at a time, HUBSPOT_TOKEN from a pinned Secret Manager version. The 'deploy' step applies tables and routines first because the function lands and CALLs them.

key_functions.name: invoker (deploy.sh)
key_functions.signature: invoker()  # gcloud scheduler jobs create http new-deals-$e --oidc-service-account-email ... --attempt-deadline 600s --max-retry-attempts 3
key_functions.does: Grants roles/run.invoker to the service account and creates the two Cloud Scheduler HTTP jobs (new-deals-SEALSQ, new-deals-ICALPS) PAUSED, with the service URL as OIDC audience; they are resumed only by 'enable' after the dry gate.

key_functions.name: patchBatch (write-back)
key_functions.does: The only async function in the repo: POSTs up to 100 deals to /crm/v3/objects/deals/batch/update, retries 429 and 5xx up to 5 times honouring the rate-limit header, parses a 207 partial result and returns one status row per deal.
key_functions.expected_output: each row gets status OK or ERROR with http_status; after 5 failed attempts: status ERROR, error 'retries exhausted'

key_functions.name: land_raw.sql (lane C landing)
key_functions.signature: INSERT INTO deals_raw ... SELECT ... TO_JSON(STRUCT(...), stringify_wide_numbers => TRUE) FROM <sync table>; DELETE older rows of the key
key_functions.does: Lane C's root writer, spliced into new_deals_weekly.sql at the marker '-- @include land_raw.sql' and reused by backfill_raw.sh: lands the 90-day set from the sync TABLE with HubSpot property names, then the labels; names raw_slice_replaced and labels_missing.

infra.detail: No asyncio: asynchrony is job-based. (1) BigQuery jobs: client.query()/load_table_from_json() submit jobs, .result(timeout=) waits, call_batch cancels on timeout. (2) Cloud Scheduler to the function is a synchronous HTTP GET (attempt deadline 600 s > service timeout 540 s, 3 retries). (3) Cloud Scheduler to the write-back is jobs.run, which returns an Operation at once, so Scheduler retries cover only start failures and the job's --max-retries 2 covers execution failures. (4) BigQuery scheduled queries run server-side with @run_time.

Cloud Run service new-deals-report (python312 base image, source build via Cloud Build), region europe-west6, private, service account new-deals-fn with bigquery.jobUser + dataset dataEditor + secretAccessor. Env var names: BQ_PROJECT, BQ_DATASET, OVERLAP_MINUTES, FIRST_RUN_DAYS, PORTAL_ID, DELIVERY_WEBHOOK_URL, ORCHESTRATOR, HUBSPOT_TOKEN (secret), DELIVERY_WEBHOOK_TOKEN (optional secret), LAND_TIMEOUT_S, CALL_TIMEOUT_S, LEASE_MINUTES.

--max-instances 1 --concurrency 1, a per-entity lease in report_state.lock_until (12 minutes), and the two entity schedules 20 minutes apart. Budget inside Cloud Run's 540 s: 4 x LAND_TIMEOUT_S (45) + CALL_TIMEOUT_S (240) + 3 delivery tries x 30 + 20 = 530 s.

DTS HubSpot sync every day 02:00 UTC; lane C scheduled queries every monday 03:53 (SEALSQ) and 04:23 (ICALPS) UTC; company tiers refresh every day 03:37 UTC; write-back job 30 5 * * 1 Europe/Zurich; lane A Scheduler jobs 0 7 * * 1 and 20 7 * * 1 Europe/Zurich. Scheduled queries are UTC and ignore DST.

Operator settings come from a gitignored .env (names listed in the file .env.example at the repository root: PROJECT, REGION, BQ_LOCATION, DATASET, FN, SA_NAME, PORTAL_ID, SYNC_DATASET, SYNC_DEALS_TABLE, SYNC_OWNERS_TABLE, SYNC_COMPANIES_TABLE, ARR_DATASET, SQL_SA_NAME, N8N_IMAGE ...). Scripts refuse placeholders. Tokens live in Secret Manager (hubspot-token read, hubspot-token-write for the job, three n8n secrets); check-env refuses a HUBSPOT_TOKEN line in .env.

BigQuery Data Transfer Service: the HubSpot connector (Preview, full refresh) fills SYNC_DATASET; scheduled queries are transfer configs with data_source scheduled_query run by service account new-deals-sql. The write-back is a Cloud Run job (node:22-slim, --tasks 1 --max-retries 2 --task-timeout 900s) started by Scheduler with an OAuth token of new-deals-scheduler.

Knative manifest applied with gcloud run services replace: pinned n8n image, Cloud SQL Postgres 17 (db-f1-micro), minScale 0 / maxScale 1, CPU always allocated, N8N_CONCURRENCY_PRODUCTION_LIMIT=1, encryption key and DB password from Secret Manager, health path /health. Workflows are imported by stable id through the n8n REST API.

ci.yml runs all offline checks on push and PR (Python 3.12, Node 22). update-readme-index.yml calls the reusable regenerate.yml to rebuild the README Documents index on pushes to main and commit it with a Regenerated-by trailer; it reads the secret named REGEN_TOKEN. Files: .github/workflows/ci.yml, regenerate.yml, update-readme-index.yml.

infra.topic: Target project of the first run
infra.detail: The operator runbook targets GCP project [id] with dataset mrload in location EU and HubSpot portal [id]; BQ_LOCATION follows the dataset's location, not the Cloud Run region. A Vertex AI Workbench instance can run the same sequence from the notebook.

decisions.decision: Run lane A (Cloud Run function) as the production orchestrator, B1 (n8n) only as its delivery tail, and add lane C's compute + write-back when the score must be visible inside HubSpot
decisions.why: A is the cheapest with the fewest parts, has the exact createdate window and the strongest guarantee set (lease, watermark after MERGE, paused-until-dry schedulers, keyless identity); only C can write back; n8n owning the whole pipeline duplicated everything.
decisions.alternative_rejected: n8n owning the whole pipeline (B2), or BigQuery scheduled queries alone as the orchestrator

decisions.decision: Fix non-reconstructible runs with a run_ts-keyed landing table (the raw root: deals_raw + labels_raw), not with another orchestrator
decisions.why: Both lanes persisted their outputs per run but never their inputs, so a past run's score, duplicates, labels and report could not be recomputed. An orchestrator sequences nodes; it does not persist the node that is missing. The three defects had one cause: inputs never landed.
decisions.alternative_rejected: A DAG/orchestrator proposal; keeping four live copies of the batch arithmetic held together by tests

decisions.decision: Store landed properties as one JSON column and type them once in the adapter view deals_landed_v1
decisions.why: Lane A delivers HubSpot strings and lane C typed sync values; the property set changes; with JSON a new property needs no DDL, old slices stay readable and 'as delivered' is kept.
decisions.alternative_rejected: 28 typed columns (every PROPS change is a migration plus a view change)

decisions.decision: Landing is plain DML outside the batch transaction, ordered load-first-then-delete-older
decisions.why: A failed batch must leave its inputs queryable, BigQuery refuses nested transactions, and a failure between the two statements must never leave an empty slice.
decisions.alternative_rejected: DELETE-then-INSERT, or landing inside the batch transaction

decisions.decision: D1: a dry run lands its slice with mode = 'dry' and writes one runs row, but no MERGE, no history, no state
decisions.why: The rehearsal becomes visible in BigQuery and only one implementation (SQL) stays alive; the convention became 'writes nothing to the sink or the state'.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Keep 'dry computes in memory and writes nothing at all', which would keep the Python shaper alive for dry only

decisions.decision: D2: lane A (the API extractor) is the root writer; lane C becomes the executor of the one SQL implementation and a fallback caller on its own state row NEW_DEALS_<entity>_C
decisions.why: HubSpot's API is what the write-back needs; sharing A's report_state key would let C rewind A, and the procedure's lease check keeps a fallback run from colliding with a live lane-A run.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Retire the DTS caller and the _C row, or share one state row

decisions.decision: D6: retire n8n B2 (NEW_DEALS_FULL, the generated Code node, the .mjs port)
decisions.why: Once the batch is one SQL implementation over the raw root that every lane CALLs, a second shaper has nothing left to mirror.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Keeping a JavaScript copy of the shaper and scorer in parity by tests

decisions.decision: Canonical deploy path gcloud run deploy --function --base-image, with the URL read from status.url
decisions.why: Google documents it as the canonical form; mixing it with the compatibility path and a cloudfunctions.net audience breaks the Scheduler OIDC audience.

decisions.decision: Audit rows are written with query INSERTs and landings with load jobs, never streaming inserts
decisions.why: A streaming buffer would block the DELETE that replaces a slice (and lane C's own DELETE in new_deals_runs).

decisions.decision: Store L2 tiers with a scheduled MERGE into a gold table (deal_tiers) plus a history table
decisions.why: The transfer may drop and recreate its destination table, which breaks a materialized view; StackSync excludes views as sources; a view holds no history; the source is a full reload, not a change stream.
decisions.alternative_rejected: Materialized view over the synced table; BigQuery CDC via the Storage Write API

gotchas.issue: Nothing has run against Google Cloud yet: pass 1, pass 2 and pass 3 are rehearsed offline only
gotchas.consequence: Every 'verified' claim is an offline test or a DRYRUN=1 rendering; the Evidence sections are empty and the first authenticated run may surface platform differences (for example strict-mode resolution of the TEMP table in the procedure).
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Follow docs/RUNBOOK_CLOUD_SHELL.md phase by phase, run tests/pass3_batch_vectors.sql in a dev dataset first, paste the probe output verbatim.

gotchas.issue: Event mode exists in code but cannot be reached: the service is private and a HubSpot workflow webhook cannot present a Google OIDC token
gotchas.consequence: The README's near-real-time path does not work as deployed; new deals appear only at the weekly window run.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Needs a relay (n8n) or a public route validating the HubSpot signature; declared out of scope for lane A.

gotchas.issue: Cloud Scheduler retries do not retry a failed write-back execution, because jobs.run returns an Operation immediately
gotchas.consequence: Scheduler sees success once the execution started; overlapping executions of the job are allowed.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: The job exits non-zero on errors so Cloud Run's --max-retries 2 re-runs it; OK rows are logged, so the retry PATCHes only the rest.

gotchas.issue: Two BigQuery scheduled scripts in the same minute are cancelled as conflicting transactions, and an on-the-hour schedule can trigger twice
gotchas.consequence: A lost or doubled lane-C run.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: scheduled_query.sh refuses a shared minute or a ':00' schedule; defaults 03:53 and 04:23 UTC.

gotchas.issue: Landing json.dumps(properties) instead of the dict stores a JSON string scalar
gotchas.consequence: Every JSON_VALUE in deals_landed_v1 reads NULL, so nothing is scored or shaped.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: land_raw passes the dict itself; test_landing_lands_the_whole_search_with_ddl_columns asserts it.

gotchas.issue: Timeout defaults drift between docs and code: parts of PASS3_RAW_ROOT.md still say LAND_TIMEOUT_S 90 s and CALL_TIMEOUT_S 300 s
gotchas.consequence: With those values the budget would exceed Cloud Run's 540 s and the request could be killed with the lease left set.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: The code and the offline test pin 45 s and 240 s (4 x 45 + 240 + 90 + 20 = 530 s).

gotchas.issue: Redeploying the write-back job resets WRITEBACK_APPROVE to the .env value (default 0)
gotchas.consequence: A live job silently goes back to dry executions that only log DRY rows.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Set WRITEBACK_APPROVE=1 in .env once the job is live.

gotchas.issue: Lane C depends on names unknown until the first transfer run, and the sync is a full refresh that overwrites its tables
gotchas.consequence: deals_synced_v1 fails to create if a column is missing; derived columns added to a sync table do not survive the next run; a past run_time reads today's sync.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Fill SYNC_* in .env after the first run; never write into a sync table; such runs carry raw_backfilled_from_current_sync; a 36 h freshness guard aborts stale runs.

gotchas.issue: A crash after the lease is taken leaves lock_until in the future
gotchas.consequence: The next run for that entity gets 409 until LEASE_MINUTES (12) have passed.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Landing and the CALL are time-boxed so failures surface inside the request and release_lease runs; deploy.sh status shows watermarks and leases.

gotchas.issue: bq --dry_run cannot execute a CALL and stops at the first IF
gotchas.consequence: DRYRUN=1 on the SQL scripts proves rendering and syntax only, not the batch logic.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Structure tests offline (tests/test_pass3_sql.py) and the executed vectors check in a dev dataset.

gotchas.issue: DATASET=mrload in the runbook puts lane A's tables next to warehouse tables
gotchas.consequence: deploy.sh tables grants dataEditor on the whole dataset to the function's service account.
gotchas.fix_or_guard: Acceptable for a first pass; a dedicated dataset (hubspot) narrows the grant at no cost.

glossary.meaning: The execution surfaces compared in the workbook: A Cloud Run function, B n8n on Cloud Run, C hybrid (BigQuery scheduled queries + write-back job), R the raw root plus the one SQL implementation every lane CALLs.
B1 = n8n only as delivery tail (webhook to XLSX to e-mail), kept. B2 = n8n owning the whole pipeline with a generated Code node, retired in pass 3 (decision D6).
deals_raw and labels_raw: a run_ts-keyed copy of what each run computed from, landed before anything is computed, so a past run is recomputable.
(run_ts, entity, orchestrator): identifies one run's rows in deals_raw, labels_raw, new_deals_history and new_deals_runs; re-landing the same key replaces the slice.
report_state.watermark per report_id (NEW_DEALS_<entity> for A, NEW_DEALS_<entity>_C for C): the end of the last successful window; it advances only after a successful MERGE.
report_state.lock_until: one run per entity at a time, taken by an atomic UPDATE; an overlapping run gets HTTP 409.
deal_id, first_seen_run, day1_hot_score, day1_hot_flag: columns the MERGE never overwrites on a re-observation or a replay.
hot_score_v1: a 0-100 logistic score of a new deal computed at first observation (fitted 2026-10-01); hot when >= 45; only for SEALSQ pipelines [id] and [id].
Normalised final customer (or first token of the deal name) used to flag duplicate suspects across pipelines and entities within 90 days.

ARRAY<STRING> on new_deals_runs naming what a run could not read or compute: sync_stale, labels_missing, dedup_horizon_partial, raw_landing_failed, raw_slice_replaced, raw_backfilled_from_current_sync, source_detail_unavailable, event_no_window.
deploy.sh dry: ?dry_run=1 for both entities; lands with mode = 'dry', one runs row, rows_written must be 0; schedulers are enabled only after it passes.
Parity words of the lane workbook: same result on every lane (pinned by a test), same result under a stated condition, or a different mechanism with a named remediation.

The 18 rows of the lane matrix: L0 deploy unit, L1 identity, L2 secrets, L3 trigger, L4 extraction window, L5 scoring, L6 shaping + duplicate flag, L7 MERGE, L8 watermark, L9 delivery, L10 write-back, L11 dry-run gate, L12 replay, L13 audit trail, L14 access control, L15 concurrency + retry safety, L16 observability, L17 cost.
Pass 1: the deploy sequence to the first weekly report. Pass 2: L2 likelihood tiers. Pass 2b: the company object by foreign-key resolution. Pass 3: the raw root and the single SQL implementation.
main.py hot_score() / shape() / name_key(): no longer in the request path, kept only to generate and check tests/hot_score_vectors.json against the SQL UDF.
A recipe is a markdown file describing one block for aider; each resulting commit carries a 'Recipe:' trailer and gets one patch in docs/diffs/ with a row in INDEX.md.
SEALSQ (pipelines [id], [id], [id], [id]; USD home currency) or ICALPS (pipeline [id]; EUR as stored).
In the notebook: executing a SQL statement from Python and showing its BigQuery job id, bytes processed and slot time next to its text.

directions: Run pass 1 for real on [id] following docs/RUNBOOK_CLOUD_SHELL.md and paste the dry-run and probe output into the empty Evidence sections: every claim is still offline.

Execute tests/pass3_batch_vectors.sql and tests/hot_score_vectors.sql in a dev dataset: the first authenticated proof that the procedure, the table function and the UDF behave as the structure tests assume.
Create the hubspot-token-write private app and run bootstrap_property.sh so lane C's write-back can go live and Breeze / workflows can read hot_score_v1 as a deal property.
Build lane W for L2 tiers (a dedicated webhook route for HubSpot's array payload with signature validation) or accept the daily cadence; the function's current event path is not it.
Register the daily tier MERGE (deal_tiers_apply.sql) as a scheduled query: scheduled_query.sh registers only the weekly script today.

Deliver the report from new_deals_last_7d or the history slice so a re-send is the same report from any lane, and decide whether to retire the DTS fallback caller and its _C state row once lane A lands reliably.
